canonical_statement: Let S be a Polish space and let (mu_n) be Borel probability measures on S converging weakly to the Borel probability measure mu. There are S-valued random variables (X_n) and X on one probability space such that X_n has law mu_n, X has law mu, and X_n converges to X almost surely.

canonical_formal_target.declaration_or_expression: planned signature using Borel probability measures on a Polish space, weak convergence, map/law equality, and almost-sure convergence

domain_and_universes: S : Type u with a Polish-space structure (metrizable, complete, separable) and its Borel measurable structure; n : Nat; probability measures mu_n and mu on S
hypotheses: mu and every muSeq n are Borel probability measures
conclusion: Existence of one probability space and measurable S-valued X and XSeq such that their laws are mu and muSeq and XSeq tends to X almost surely
degenerate_and_boundary_cases: Constant sequences and Dirac measures remain in scope. No atomlessness, Euclidean structure, or convergence in probability is substituted for almost-sure convergence. The common probability space is existential and is not required to be the original space of any pre-existing variables.
